content.text:
**Verdict: pass.** Every check I ran came back green; the findings below are missing coverage and stale comments, not failures.

## What ran

Repo: `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek`, branch `main`, four modified files uncommitted (`tui.c`, `tests/tui.sh`, `sst.doc`, `README.md`); nothing staged, nothing untracked. Worktree is exactly as I found it — I reconfigured `build-debug`/`build-release` and restored their `SST_WERROR=ON` cache afterwards; all other work was in `/tmp` copies.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cmake -S . -B build-debug -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug && cmake --build build-debug` | clean, 0 warnings |
| same for Release | clean, 0 warnings |
| both build types again with `-DSST_WERROR=ON` (per #125, since `verifier.md` does not yet ask for it) | clean |
| `ctest --test-dir build-debug --output-on-failure` | 11/11 passed, 257 s |
| `ctest --test-dir build-release --output-on-failure` | 11/11 passed, 248 s |
| `tests/tui.sh ./build-debug/sst Debug` standalone rerun | passed |
| `tests/tui.sh` in a clean `/tmp` copy of the worktree | passed |
| `shellcheck -s sh tests/tui.sh` vs `main`'s copy | both clean, no new findings |
| `gcc -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion` on `tui.c` vs `main`'s `tui.c` | one new warning (below) |
| plain mode vs a build of `main` (`git archive main`): setup/scan/quit journey, tournament journey through `rest 5000`→`y`, `TERM=dumb -t` fallback | byte-identical; `golden` passing in both configs is the byte-for-byte check |

Four `tui.sh` runs, no flakes. Every failure I saw was deterministic (each mutant below failed identically on its named assertion).

## Mutation testing of the fix

Eleven mutants, each in a fresh `/tmp` copy with its own `build/`, run as `tests/tui.sh <copy>/build/sst Debug`. **Killed 8, survived 3.**

Killed — the suite really does test the fix:

| Mutant | Caught by |
|---|---|
| restore the removed `pending_answer` gate (full revert) | `ended: after 20x8 / 80x14 / 80x23 …` — all three sizes |
| `arows = 0` (never step back over the answer's rows) | 80x23 block + wrapping block |
| `arows` capped at 1 | `wrapped answer: at 80x24 …` only |
| disable the answer-prefix skip in the tail test | 80x23 block + wrapping block |
| demand the whole answer instead of the on-screen prefix | `wrapped answer: at 80x23 …` |
| `want` = question+answer joined (failed attempt 1) | 80x23 + wrapping |
| `want` = question+padding+answer (failed attempt 2) | 80x23 + wrapping |

Both of your failing-first rounds reproduce independently: mutant 1 fails at all three drag sizes, and the wrapping block is the *only* thing that catches the one-row `arows` cap.

Survived:

- **The three exact-fill guards are untested.** Removing `i % width != 0` at `tui.c:554`, `linelen % width != 0` at `tui.c:669`, and `linelen % oldmsgw != 0` at `tui.c:610` each leaves the suite green. They are not equivalent mutants — I reproduced visible differences by hand. The prompt `" Are you sure?"` is 14 characters (instrumented build: `linelen=14`), so exact fill needs a message window of 14 or 7 columns, i.e. a terminal of 16 or 9 columns. At 80x24→16x24 the `:554` mutant garbles the screen where the fixed build restores cleanly:

  ```
  fixed:   COMMAND> rest 5      mutant:   COMMAND> rest
           Are you sure?                  Are you sure? 5
           y                              y
  ```
  and dragging 16→12→9 shows the `:669` and `:610` mutants diverging too (instrumentation confirms `nl=0` and `pad=0` fire at those steps). All of it is below the documented 72-column minimum, which is #94's territory — so this is low-severity untested-but-live code, not a defect.

- **An ended line restored while a *pause* waits has no coverage.** Adding `if (pending_answer == NULL) return;` right after `ended = TRUE` leaves the whole suite green. That path is live: `pause(1)` in `sst.c:772-775` writes `[ANNOUNCEMENT ARRIVING...]` / `[IMPORTANT ANNOUNCEMENT ARRIVING -- HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` with `prout` and then `getch()`, so `ended` is true and `pending_answer` is NULL. `tui.sh`'s existing resize-pause block uses the help pager, which is `proutn("[CONTINUE?]")` — a `curline` case, not this one. The gap predates this change (it arrived with #112), but the change rewrites how `want` is built for exactly that case, so nothing guards the rewrite.

## Reachability and comments in `restore_curline()`

Nothing became unreachable. Two comments now describe behavior the change removed, and both are unchanged from `main`:

- `tui.c:356` — `cursor_at_prompt`'s comment still says a prompt that ended its own line "was not kept -- see lastline, which covers most of those now, **and #117 for the case it does not**." There is no such case any more; what is left is a window too short, which the comment does not say.
- `tests/tui.sh:1371-1375` — the comment introducing the block you rewrote still reads "once the answer is part typed, the question is **left alone** -- #117 -- which has to be asserted as 'never more than one', **not as a restore**", directly above the assertion that now demands the restore. The inner comment at 1396 was updated; this outer one was not.

Two smaller notes, both about code the diff touched:

- Of the three exact-fill guards, only `tui.c:610` carries a note ("Guarded like the padding above"). `tui.c:554` and `tui.c:669` acquired the `% width != 0` condition with no comment, so the narrative that "three places are guarded" is only visible in one of them.
- `tui.c:502`'s `width > 0` conjunct can never be false — it sits inside `if (r >= 0 && width > 0)` at `tui.c:461`. Harmless, but it reads as a live guard.
- New `-Wshadow` warning (not in the project's flag set, so CI stays green): `int alen` at `tui.c:510` shadows `int alen` at `tui.c:473`. Same value in that branch, so not a bug.

## Documentation

- **CRLF:** all 25 added `sst.doc` lines end `\r\n`; none was added bare-LF.
- **Width:** maximum 70 columns excluding the CR — four lines land on exactly 70 (`whatever you had typed of an answer to it -- but look at both before`, `first word of your answer and only its first letter, so an "N" typed`, `characters. Where the terminal cannot grow, do not answer and do not`, `"N", never repeating what it wanted; answer N to decline whatever it`), the rest ≤69. If the rule is "under 70" those four are over by one; nothing in the repo enforces a width, the file's own maximum is 79, and the section already contained a 73. `git diff --check` flags every added line as trailing whitespace — that is the CR, and `sst.doc` is not listed in `.gitattributes`, so it happens on any edit to this file.
- **Manual vs game, measured.** Your residual numbers reproduce exactly at 72 columns with a 90-character answer: 72x17 and 72x16 restore both; 72x15 keeps the whole answer and loses the question; 72x14 leaves a 34-character fragment. Growing back one row at a time restores the answer at 15 and the question at 16 — so "give the terminal another row or two" and "the question comes back with your typing untouched" are both literally true.
- **Manual vs README:** they agree, and the paragraph at `README.md:16-21` that this change did *not* touch ("both the question you were asked and the answer you were halfway through typing survive, so long as there is still room for them") was an overclaim on `main` and becomes true with the fix.
- One accuracy point: `sst.doc:1591` says "the self-destruct password **is** nine characters". `setup.c:532` prompts "Please type in a secret password (9 characters maximum)-" and `sst.h:279` declares `passwd[10]`, so it is up to nine and the player chooses it. The argument the sentence is making (retyping is a nuisance) survives the correction.
- Pagination: the section's "page" grows 127→133 lines between form feeds, already by far the longest in the file (others 47-67) on `main`. No regression, and `help` and `instructions` both pass.

## Journey coverage I ran by hand

All against `./build-debug/sst`, each in tmux on its own `-L` socket with `-f /dev/null`, cleaned up with `kill-server` on that socket only.

- 13-step slow drag 80x24→72x20→80x24 with a one-character answer: exactly one question at every step, no stacking.
- Width drag 80→78→76→74→72→80 with the 90-character answer: one question per step, and the full 90 characters restored across two rows at the end. **No test covers this** — the new block drags height only, and the three-size block does one width step with a one-character answer. It passes, but nothing guards it.
- Small-window robustness, 90-character answer through 80x14, 80x13, 72x14, 72x24, 80x15, 80x24: never more than one question, no crash, no garbling, and on return the pair is whole. Then Ctrl-U → `n` → `COMMAND>`, then `quit` → score → play-again, so the game exits cleanly after the drag.
- The self-destruct prompt, a longer ended line (`SELF-DESTRUCT-SEQUENCE-WILL-BE-ABORTED` after `prout` at `finish.c:24`): typed `zz`, dragged 80x23 / 80x24 / 76x20 / 80x24 / 72x24 — prompt and answer each present exactly once at every step, and Enter then reaches `PASSWORD-REJECTED` and returns to `COMMAND>`.

## Environment issues

- **No `cppcheck`, `clang-tidy`, `scan-build`, or `valgrind` installed**, and no `clang`. The static pass was therefore compiler warnings only: the project's `-Wall -Wextra -Wmissing-prototypes` (clean), `-Werror` (clean), and an extra `-Wshadow -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion` run diffed against `main` (one new warning). `shellcheck` is present and clean. Treat the analyzer pass as not run, not as a pass.
- **gcov coverage of `restore_curline()` could not be collected.** A `--coverage` build run through `tests/tui.sh` produced a `tui.c.gcda` recording exactly one process — `make_windows` count 1, the whole of `restore_curline` `#####` — because the tmux sessions are torn down rather than exited, so the resizing processes never flush. Scripted clean-exit runs did not flush either. I substituted the mutation battery above and an `fprintf`-instrumented build (in a `/tmp` copy) for the branch-level questions.

## Reproducing

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-debug  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug   -DSST_WERROR=ON && cmake --build build-debug
cmake -S . -B build-release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSST_WERROR=ON && cmake --build build-release
ctest --test-dir build-debug --output-on-failure
ctest --test-dir build-release --output-on-failure
printf 'regular\nshort\nnovice\nxyz\nsrscan\nlrscan\nstatus\ndamages\nchart\nquit\nn\n' | ./build-debug/sst
```

cd /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek
cat > "$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/i8.md" <<'EOF'
`restore_curline()` has a branch for a prompt that ended its own line, reached
when `curlen == 0` and a reader is waiting. Two different readers can be
waiting there, and only one of them is covered:

- `tui_readline()` sets `pending_answer` to the buffer before it repaints, so
  it is non-NULL — an empty string when nothing has been typed yet.
- `tui_getch()` does not, so `pending_answer` is NULL.

Every ended-prompt case in `tests/tui.sh` goes through the first. The second is
a `pause(1)`, and nothing in the suite reaches one.

## How it was found

The `verifier` mutated `tui.c` with

```c
if (pending_answer == NULL) return;
```

immediately after `ended = TRUE`, and the whole suite stayed green — 11/11 in
both configurations. That mutant disables the restore for exactly the
`tui_getch()` case.

## Why it matters

`pause(1)` is the announcement pause: `sst.c:770-776` writes
`[ANNOUNCEMENT ARRIVING...]` or
`[IMPORTANT ANNOUNCEMENT ARRIVING -- HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` with `prout`
and then calls `getch()`. `prout` appends the newline, so `curline` is empty
and this is an ended line by construction — the same shape #112 was about. A
resize there with the restore broken leaves the player looking at a screen with
no prompt on it, waiting on a keystroke they have not been asked for.

The existing resize-during-a-pause coverage does not reach it: `tui.sh` uses
the help pager, which is `proutn("[CONTINUE?]")` / `proutn("[HIT SPACE BAR TO
CONTINUE]")` at `sst.c:778-782` — a `curline` case, not this one.

## Why it is not covered

`pause(1)` is only called from `ai.c:354`, `:516` and `:565`, all of them
inside starbase-under-attack and Super-commander announcements. Reaching one
deterministically means driving the game to an event rather than issuing a
command, which is why the gap has stood since #112 introduced the branch.

## Fix sketch

A seeded tournament game whose early events include one of those
announcements would do it — `tests/tournament.sh` already plays fourteen fixed
seeds and asserts against what they produce, so the machinery for finding a
seed that reaches a given event exists. Find one, drive it to the announcement
in `tests/tui.sh`, resize during the pause, and assert the prompt is on screen
exactly once afterwards.

Failing that, `#ifdef DEBUG` already gates other test affordances; a way to
force the announcement would make the branch reachable without hunting a seed.

## Provenance

Reported by the `verifier` as a surviving mutant while verifying the fix for
#117, which rewrites how `want` is built for this branch. The gap predates that
change — it arrived with #112 — so it is filed rather than fixed there, per
AGENTS.md step 9.
EOF
gh issue create --title "Nothing covers restore_curline()'s ended-prompt branch at a pause" --body-file "$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/i8.md"

## Verdict: pass

The change builds, the whole suite passes, and the three claims you asked me to check hold — with four documentation nits, one of which I missed on my previous pass.

### Answers to your three questions

**1. Are the comment edits accurate now?**

*Yes on the substance.* I confirmed the behaviour the `cursor_at_prompt` comment and the docs now describe, by hand, in tmux:

| shape | message window | what is on screen |
|---|---|---|
| 80x24 | 10 rows | ` Are you sure?` / ` y` — pair, once each |
| 80x15 | 2 rows | the wrapping answer's two rows, **question gone** |
| 80x14 | 1 row | short answer: ` Are you sure? y` on one row; wrapping answer: **tail of the answer only** |
| 80x13 | 0 rows | nothing (covered by the earlier README/`sst.doc` paragraph) |

So "down to a window too short to hold the question and the answer together, where what survives is the answer" is true, and "shorter still only part of that" is true. Growing back restored the pair with the answer intact, the cursor landed after it (typed `zz` appended as `yzz`), and Enter took the answer.

`tests/tui.sh`'s rewritten block comment now matches the assertion under it: question exactly once, answer `y` on the row below, asserted as the pair.

*Nits, in `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c` and `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tests/tui.sh`:*

- **The "ninety characters" figure is wrong in two places** — `tui.c:472` ("an answer of ninety characters at eighty columns takes two") and `tests/tui.sh:1434` ("90 characters at 80 columns"). The literal the test sends is `y` + 86 `b`s = **87** characters. The reasoning survives (87 > the 78-column message window, so two rows, and the screen confirms 78 + 9), but the number a later reader would check against is off by three. This was present before my last pass; I did not catch it then.
- **"And the third of the same guard"** (the `waddch` newline guard) counts three `% width` guards. A reader counting all of them finds four: the `bound` padding, the cursor rounding, the `linelen % oldmsgw` filler at the erase (whose own comment already says "Guarded like the padding above"), and this one.
- The `cursor_at_prompt` paragraph still has the ragged short line `* false where no` — the edit fixed the stray indent but not the wrap.
- Strictly, in the too-short case `cursor_at_prompt` is still set `TRUE` (the restore runs and places the cursor). The new clause reads as a limit on how far coverage extends, which is right; it could be read as naming a case where the flag is false, which it is not.
- The shape the clause describes is only reachable at 15 or 14 rows — below the documented 24-row minimum, the same territory as #94. Not wrong (the docs describe 13/14/15-row behaviour elsewhere), just worth knowing it is not reachable at a supported size.

**2. Did removing the inner `alen` and the `width > 0` conjunct change behaviour? No.**

- `width` is assigned exactly once (`width = getmaxx(wmsg)`) and never reassigned; the `if (ended)` block sits inside `if (r >= 0 && width > 0)`. The conjunct was a tautology there, so its removal cannot change anything.
- Inside `if (ended)`, the surviving outer `alen` is `ended && pending_answer != NULL ? strlen(pending_answer) : 0`, i.e. exactly `pending_answer != NULL ? strlen(...) : 0`. Nothing between the declaration and the uses touches `pending_answer` (`mvwinnstr`, `strncat`, `strstr` only). It stays NULL-safe: `strncmp` is gated on `alen > 0`.
- I also reconstructed the pre-edit text in `/tmp` and diffed `-O0`/`-O2` assembly. That comparison is **not** decisive evidence — the prior text is not in git, so I had to guess it, and the diff is register allocation, label numbering and one redundant `strlen` the shadow forced. The static argument above plus the suite and the mutants below is what the conclusion rests on.
- `-Wshadow` on `tui.c` reports only `draw_quad_line:150` and `draw_status_line:160`, both pre-existing `chtype a` vs `sst.h:170`. Your note named only the first; there are two, neither from this diff.

**3. Is the rewrapped `sst.doc` paragraph true and well formed? Yes.**

- CRLF throughout, **zero** bare-LF lines; every added line is ≤ 70 columns (widths 61-70, matching the surrounding prose). The only >70 line in the region is the pre-existing `ACKNOWLEDGMENTS` header, whose length counts its form feed.
- "the self-destruct password can be nine characters" matches `setup.c:532` (`"Please type in a secret password (9 characters maximum)-"`) and `sst.h:279` (`passwd[10]`).
- "a window left too short to hold the pair keeps the answer and loses the question above it" matches the 80x15 observation above; "shorter still only a piece of that" matches 80x14.
- The "Modifications I made" page is now 133 lines between form feeds, up from 127 on `main`. It was already the one unpaginated page in the file, so this is not introduced by the change.

### Failures
None. No flakes: `tests/tui.sh` ran clean three times (Debug ctest, Release ctest, and directly), and two mutant runs produced only their targeted failures.

### Missing coverage
- **Width drag with a wrapping answer** — still no automated test. I ran it: 80→79…→72→…→80 at 24 rows, question on screen exactly once at every one of thirteen steps, answer stable at two rows, cursor correct afterwards (`zzz` appended cleanly). **My judgment: this should not block.** `arows` is killed by the height-drag test (mutant M1 below), and the width-drag block's answer assertion is already filed as #115 — a line on #115 is the right home for it, not a new test in this slice.
- **The too-short shapes themselves (80x15, 80x14) are asserted nowhere.** The squeeze loop passes through `80 14` but only asserts after growing back to 80x24, so the exact behaviour the new doc paragraph and the new `tui.c` comment describe is documented but untested. I verified it by hand this round. Worth a note on #94.
- The pause path (`pending_answer == NULL` after `ended = TRUE`) is filed as #134 — I did not re-attempt it.

### Environment issues
- **No static analyser is installed**: `cppcheck`, `clang-tidy` and `scan-build` are all absent. That check did not run; I substituted a `-Wshadow -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion` rebuild through CMake, which shows no warning anywhere in `restore_curline`.
- **I have to report an accident of my own.** In one compound command I mistakenly included `git stash push --keep-index --include-untracked`, which stashed your four modified files. I noticed immediately and ran `git stash pop`. The tree is restored: `git status` shows the same four modified files, `git diff --stat` shows the identical `23/44/74/129` line counts I reviewed at the start, and `git stash list` is empty. Nothing else in the repository was written to; all builds, mutants and copies were made under `/tmp`.

### What ran
- `cmake -S . -B /tmp/vb-debug -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DSST_WERROR=ON` + build — clean; same for `Release` in `/tmp/vb-release`.
- `ctest --output-on-failure` in both: **11/11 passed** each (Debug 257s, Release 248s), including `tui`, `tournament`, `golden`.
- `tests/tui.sh /tmp/vb-debug/sst Debug` directly — `tui OK`, third clean run.
- `sh -n` and `shellcheck -s sh` on `tests/tui.sh` — clean.
- CMake rebuild with `-Wshadow -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion`; `-Werror` builds via `SST_WERROR=ON`.
- **Mutation, in a copy at `/tmp/mut-tree` configured fresh (never in the repo):** M1 `arows = alen > 0 ? 1 : 0` → killed by `wrapped answer: at 80x24 the question is not on screen exactly once`; M2 disabling the answer-prefix skip → killed by both `ended: after 80x23 the question and its part-typed answer are not both back, once each` and `wrapped answer: at 80x23...`. Different mutants gave different failures, which also confirms the copy builds from copied sources.
- **Journeys**, tmux on my own socket `-L sst-verify -f /dev/null`, server killed on that socket only: part-typed answer through 80x14/13/12 and back; wrapping answer through 80x16/15/14 and back, then Enter (answer read as `y`, game ran to its ending); width drag 80→72→80 with a wrapping answer plus a cursor-placement check; 80x15 cursor and grow-placement check; 72x24 with squeezes to 72x14, 72x23, 60x20 and back, then through the endgame and `quit`. No crash, hang or garbled output.
- Plain mode: `printf 'regular\nshort\nnovice\nxyz\nsrscan\nstatus\nquit\nn\n' | sst` — exit 0, no CR in output; the `golden` fixtures are untouched by the diff and pass, which is the stronger guarantee that plain mode is byte-identical.

### Answers to your three questions

**1. Are the comment edits accurate now?**

*Yes on the substance.* I confirmed the behaviour the `cursor_at_prompt` comment and the docs now describe, by hand, in tmux:

| shape | message window | what is on screen |
|---|---|---|
| 80x24 | 10 rows | ` Are you sure?` / ` y` — pair, once each |
| 80x15 | 2 rows | the wrapping answer's two rows, **question gone** |
| 80x14 | 1 row | short answer: ` Are you sure? y` on one row; wrapping answer: **tail of the answer only** |
| 80x13 | 0 rows | nothing (covered by the earlier README/`sst.doc` paragraph) |

So "down to a window too short to hold the question and the answer together, where what survives is the answer" is true, and "shorter still only part of that" is true. Growing back restored the pair with the answer intact, the cursor landed after it (typed `zz` appended as `yzz`), and Enter took the answer.

`tests/tui.sh`'s rewritten block comment now matches the assertion under it: question exactly once, answer `y` on the row below, asserted as the pair.

*Nits, in `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c` and `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tests/tui.sh`:*

- **The "ninety characters" figure is wrong in two places** — `tui.c:472` ("an answer of ninety characters at eighty columns takes two") and `tests/tui.sh:1434` ("90 characters at 80 columns"). The literal the test sends is `y` + 86 `b`s = **87** characters. The reasoning survives (87 > the 78-column message window, so two rows, and the screen confirms 78 + 9), but the number a later reader would check against is off by three. This was present before my last pass; I did not catch it then.
- **"And the third of the same guard"** (the `waddch` newline guard) counts three `% width` guards. A reader counting all of them finds four: the `bound` padding, the cursor rounding, the `linelen % oldmsgw` filler at the erase (whose own comment already says "Guarded like the padding above"), and this one.
- The `cursor_at_prompt` paragraph still has the ragged short line `* false where no` — the edit fixed the stray indent but not the wrap.
- Strictly, in the too-short case `cursor_at_prompt` is still set `TRUE` (the restore runs and places the cursor). The new clause reads as a limit on how far coverage extends, which is right; it could be read as naming a case where the flag is false, which it is not.

**2. Did removing the inner `alen` and the `width > 0` conjunct change behaviour? No.**

- `width` is assigned exactly once (`width = getmaxx(wmsg)`) and never reassigned; the `if (ended)` block sits inside `if (r >= 0 && width > 0)`. The conjunct was a tautology there, so its removal cannot change anything.
- Inside `if (ended)`, the surviving outer `alen` is `ended && pending_answer != NULL ? strlen(pending_answer) : 0`, i.e. exactly `pending_answer != NULL ? strlen(...) : 0`. Nothing between the declaration and the uses touches `pending_answer` (`mvwinnstr`, `strncat`, `strstr` only). It stays NULL-safe: `strncmp` is gated on `alen > 0`.

That comparison is **not** decisive evidence — the prior text is not in git, so I had to guess it, and the diff is register allocation, label numbering and one redundant `strlen` the shadow forced. The static argument above plus the suite and the mutants below is what the conclusion rests on.
- `-Wshadow` on `tui.c` reports only `draw_quad_line:150` and `draw_status_line:160`, both pre-existing `chtype a` vs `sst.h:170`. Your note named only the first; there are two, neither from this diff.

- CRLF throughout, **zero** bare-LF lines; every added line is ≤ 70 columns (widths 61-70, matching the surrounding prose). The only >70 line in the region is the pre-existing `ACKNOWLEDGMENTS` header, whose length counts its form feed.

**The defect.** `restore_curline()` refused to restore a prompt that ended its own line once the player had begun typing an answer. The gate was deliberate: two earlier attempts at spanning the row boundary between an ended prompt and its answer each duplicated the question, one per width step in the first and once on a one-row height shrink in the second.

**Why it matters to a player.** On a one-row height shrink `wresize()` cuts the answer's row and keeps the question's, so the screen reads as a clean unanswered question while the reader still holds the typed `y`. I reproduced the whole thing: typing `N` there submits `yN`, `ja()` takes the `y`, `rest 5000` runs, and the game ends with "Your time has run out and the Federation has been conquered."

**The fix** — the second of the two options the issue's fix sketch offers, model two rows rather than one:
- `want` is the question alone for an ended line; a single joined string can only match all or none of the pair, and a height shrink leaves half of it on screen
- the read-back steps back over every row the answer takes
- the tail test steps over curses' padding and then over as much of the answer as is on screen — a prefix, since the shrink truncates it
- three places that rounded up to the next row boundary unconditionally are guarded for a question that fills its row exactly

The fix does **not** discard the buffered `y`; it makes it visible. Typing `N` after a resize still answers yes. That is the player's to clear and the manual says how.

**`verifier` ran twice, both pass.** It mutated the fix itself rather than trusting me: **8 mutants killed, 3 survived**. Killed include full reverts of the gate, `arows = 0`, `arows` capped at 1, disabling the answer-prefix skip, demanding the whole answer, and both historical failed attempts at `want`. Survivors: two exact-fill guards reachable only at 16 or 9 columns (below the documented minimum, commented on #94) and the pause path, filed as **#134**. It also caught a shadowed variable, a dead `width > 0` conjunct, two stale comments, and a wrong "ninety characters" figure — the literal is 87 — all fixed.

content.text:
## Verdict: request changes

Reviewed state: branch `fix/117-restore-ended-prompt` at HEAD `8fbb4db` (no commits on the branch), plus the four unstaged files — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c`, `tests/tui.sh`, `sst.doc`, `README.md`. Nothing staged, nothing untracked.

What I ran: `-DSST_WERROR=ON` build clean; `ctest -E tui` 8/8; `tests/tui.sh` green; your `'ybbb'` mutation reproduced out of the repository — exactly the two new assertions fail and nothing else, question counts stay green, so the non-blindness proof holds.

One blocker, found by driving the change on a wide terminal.

---

### Blocker

**`tui.c:413`, with `tui.c:463-489` — on a message window wider than 511 columns the joined-row search reads a truncated row, so the ended-plus-answer path never matches and every resize takes the rewrite path.**

`mvwinnstr(wmsg, rr, 0, onscreen, (int)sizeof onscreen - 1)` returns at most 511 characters, but the whole search depends on each appended row being exactly `width` columns — that is what makes `start`, `skip % width`, `bound` and `i / width` mean columns. Above 511 the strings stop lining up: the question's row-padding runs into the answer's first character at offset 511 instead of at `bound`, the tail test fails, and the code falls through to the branch that scrolls and writes without erasing.

Before this change `tui.c:433-436` returned early whenever an answer was part typed, so this path could not be entered. It can now, and it is the "copies up the window" failure the comparison exists to prevent.

Reproduced at 600x24 (`rest 5000`, type an answer, drag height 24→23→24→23→24), against `./build/sst` built from this worktree:

- One-character answer `y`: the question count goes 1, **0**, 1, **0**, 1, and the final screen is

  ```
   COMMAND> rest 5000
   yre you sure?

   yre you sure?

   Are you sure?
   y
  ```

  `yre you sure?` is the echo typed over column 0 of the restored question — the exact corruption the comment at `tui.c:546-553` describes — stacked twice.
- 87-character answer: three orphan copies of the typed answer up the window with a single question; at 600x23 the question is gone.
- Same journey with `main`'s `tui.c` dropped into a copy of the tree: question exactly once at every step, no corruption (the answer is simply not restored, i.e. #117 itself).
- Same journey with only `char onscreen[2048] … joined[8192]` changed in a copy of this branch: correct at every step, pair intact.

That last run is the diagnosis, not a proposed patch. Terminal width ≥ 514 columns is what it takes (`width = COLS - 2`), which an ultrawide or high-DPI terminal at a small font reaches.

Suggested fix: make the invariant explicit rather than incidental — read each row into a buffer that can hold `width` columns and pad a short read out to `width` before appending, sizing `joined` from that; and where a row genuinely cannot be read whole, return without writing (what `main` did) rather than falling through to the rewrite path, since that path is what stacks copies. The comment at `tui.c:405-412` is what would have caught this and should be corrected with it: "nothing the game writes reaches column 255" is a statement about *content*, but the join needs each row's full width, blanks included.

Since this is a `tui.c` change it re-triggers `verifier` and a fresh `code-review`. On `ui-review`: the fix makes already-reviewed behaviour appear at a width no round exercised, so a stated skip with that reasoning would be defensible — but state it, don't omit it.

---

### Should-fix

**`tests/tui.sh:1517-1533` — the wrapping block never presses Enter, so nothing in the suite checks that the restored answer is the one the reader holds. This one belongs in the slice, not in #135.**

Every neighbouring block in this file carries that control and says why it is there — `N Enter` at line ~1355 ("it would fail a fix that reprinted the question by re-asking it and left two readers stacked"), `Space` at ~1249 for the pause. The new block is the one where the restore does the most work — it `wmove`s into the middle of the window and relies on the echo rewriting the answer there — and it is the only one without a control. It is also the block whose claim is the one `sst.doc` and `README.md` now make to the player: what is on screen is what the game will act on.

It costs four lines at the end of a session that is already open at 80x24, and I exercised it by hand: after the drag, Enter takes the `y` and the game rests to the end of the game (`It is stardate 4807.7`, then the ending text and `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]`). So the assertion is "the question is gone and the rest happened", and nothing after it depends on the session, since the next block calls `start`.

On the rest of #135: deferring the two exact-fill guard tests is the right call, and the issue is well written. One correction worth adding as a comment there — its rationale says the guards "fire only below 72 columns", but the condition is `linelen % width == 0`, which also fires for an ended line of exactly 70, 78, 140 … at supported widths. It happens to be true today: the longest `prout` immediately preceding a reader is around 64 characters and the pause literal is 61, so no pending ended line reaches 70. Recording *that* is what keeps the deferral honest the day someone writes a 70-character prompt.

---

### On the review-coverage answer: accepted

Your claim survives both readings of it. Taken at face value — comments, a shadowed `alen`, a dead conjunct — none of it reaches a screen. Taken at its weakest, if the two guards themselves post-dated round 3, `#135`'s own mutation evidence puts their visible effect at 16 and 9 columns, below anything a `ui-review` round would have covered. Either way no fourth round was owed, and saying so before the commit is the disclosure step 8 asks for.

Two caveats, neither of which changes the verdict. The branch has no commits, so the round-3 state is unrecoverable from the worktree and I judged the claim from the final code and a green `tui.sh` rather than by diffing what that round saw. And the blocker above is a reminder of what the split buys you: three `ui-review` rounds and five `verifier` rounds all ran at 72-80 columns, which is where the instructions point them, and the defect lives at 600.

---

### Not reviewed

- The states `ui-review` rounds 1-3 actually saw — no commits exist for them.
- A corner drag (width and height together) with a pending answer: `rows` at `tui.c:600-620` is computed from the old layout, while a simultaneous height shrink can have cut some of those rows, in which case the erase at `tui.c:629-632` starts too high and takes live conversation with it. I did not reproduce it and nothing asserts it; it would show *during* the drag, not after. Worth a look before it is written off.

## Verdict: request changes

Reviewed state: branch `fix/117-restore-ended-prompt` at HEAD `8fbb4db` (no commits on the branch), plus the four unstaged files — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c`, `tests/tui.sh`, `sst.doc`, `README.md`. Nothing staged, nothing untracked.

What I ran: `-DSST_WERROR=ON` build clean; `ctest -E tui` 8/8; `tests/tui.sh` green; your `'ybbb'` mutation reproduced out of the repository — exactly the two new assertions fail and nothing else, question counts stay green, so the non-blindness proof holds.

One blocker, found by driving the change on a wide terminal.

---

### Blocker

**`tui.c:413`, with `tui.c:463-489` — on a message window wider than 511 columns the joined-row search reads a truncated row, so the ended-plus-answer path never matches and every resize takes the rewrite path.**

`mvwinnstr(wmsg, rr, 0, onscreen, (int)sizeof onscreen - 1)` returns at most 511 characters, but the whole search depends on each appended row being exactly `width` columns — that is what makes `start`, `skip % width`, `bound` and `i / width` mean columns. Above 511 the strings stop lining up: the question's row-padding runs into the answer's first character at offset 511 instead of at `bound`, the tail test fails, and the code falls through to the branch that scrolls and writes without erasing.

Before this change `tui.c:433-436` returned early whenever an answer was part typed, so this path could not be entered. It can now, and it is the "copies up the window" failure the comparison exists to prevent.

Reproduced at 600x24 (`rest 5000`, type an answer, drag height 24→23→24→23→24), against `./build/sst` built from this worktree:

- One-character answer `y`: the question count goes 1, **0**, 1, **0**, 1, and the final screen is

  ```
   COMMAND> rest 5000
   yre you sure?

   yre you sure?

   Are you sure?
   y
  ```

  `yre you sure?` is the echo typed over column 0 of the restored question — the exact corruption the comment at `tui.c:546-553` describes — stacked twice.
- 87-character answer: three orphan copies of the typed answer up the window with a single question; at 600x23 the question is gone.
- Same journey with `main`'s `tui.c` dropped into a copy of the tree: question exactly once at every step, no corruption (the answer is simply not restored, i.e. #117 itself).
- Same journey with only `char onscreen[2048] … joined[8192]` changed in a copy of this branch: correct at every step, pair intact.

That last run is the diagnosis, not a proposed patch. Terminal width ≥ 514 columns is what it takes (`width = COLS - 2`), which an ultrawide or high-DPI terminal at a small font reaches.

Suggested fix: make the invariant explicit rather than incidental — read each row into a buffer that can hold `width` columns and pad a short read out to `width` before appending, sizing `joined` from that; and where a row genuinely cannot be read whole, return without writing (what `main` did) rather than falling through to the rewrite path, since that path is what stacks copies. The comment at `tui.c:405-412` is what would have caught this and should be corrected with it: "nothing the game writes reaches column 255" is a statement about *content*, but the join needs each row's full width, blanks included.

Since this is a `tui.c` change it re-triggers `verifier` and a fresh `code-review`. On `ui-review`: the fix makes already-reviewed behaviour appear at a width no round exercised, so a stated skip with that reasoning would be defensible — but state it, don't omit it.

---

### Should-fix

**`tests/tui.sh:1517-1533` — the wrapping block never presses Enter, so nothing in the suite checks that the restored answer is the one the reader holds. This one belongs in the slice, not in #135.**

Every neighbouring block in this file carries that control and says why it is there — `N Enter` at line ~1355 ("it would fail a fix that reprinted the question by re-asking it and left two readers stacked"), `Space` at ~1249 for the pause. The new block is the one where the restore does the most work — it `wmove`s into the middle of the window and relies on the echo rewriting the answer there — and it is the only one without a control. It is also the block whose claim is the one `sst.doc` and `README.md` now make to the player: what is on screen is what the game will act on.

It costs four lines at the end of a session that is already open at 80x24, and I exercised it by hand: after the drag, Enter takes the `y` and the game rests to the end of the game (`It is stardate 4807.7`, then the ending text and `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]`). So the assertion is "the question is gone and the rest happened", and nothing after it depends on the session, since the next block calls `start`.

On the rest of #135: deferring the two exact-fill guard tests is the right call, and the issue is well written. One correction worth adding as a comment there — its rationale says the guards "fire only below 72 columns", but the condition is `linelen % width == 0`, which also fires for an ended line of exactly 70, 78, 140 … at supported widths. It happens to be true today: the longest `prout` immediately preceding a reader is around 64 characters and the pause literal is 61, so no pending ended line reaches 70. Recording *that* is what keeps the deferral honest the day someone writes a 70-character prompt.

---

### On the review-coverage answer: accepted

Your claim survives both readings of it. Taken at face value — comments, a shadowed `alen`, a dead conjunct — none of it reaches a screen. Taken at its weakest, if the two guards themselves post-dated round 3, `#135`'s own mutation evidence puts their visible effect at 16 and 9 columns, below anything a `ui-review` round would have covered. Either way no fourth round was owed, and saying so before the commit is the disclosure step 8 asks for.

Two caveats, neither of which changes the verdict. The branch has no commits, so the round-3 state is unrecoverable from the worktree and I judged the claim from the final code and a green `tui.sh` rather than by diffing what that round saw. And the blocker above is a reminder of what the split buys you: three `ui-review` rounds and five `verifier` rounds all ran at 72-80 columns, which is where the instructions point them, and the defect lives at 600.

---

### Not reviewed

- The states `ui-review` rounds 1-3 actually saw — no commits exist for them.
- A corner drag (width and height together) with a pending answer: `rows` at `tui.c:600-620` is computed from the old layout, while a simultaneous height shrink can have cut some of those rows, in which case the erase at `tui.c:629-632` starts too high and takes live conversation with it. I did not reproduce it and nothing asserts it; it would show *during* the drag, not after. Worth a look before it is written off.
A real blocker at 600 columns — my change made a truncation bug reachable. Fixing it, plus the Enter control.

content.text:
## Verdict: **FAIL**

One deterministic regression against `main`, and the guard that this round exists to add has no test.

---

## Failures

### 1. The guard's `return` leaves the cursor parked on the question — deterministic, reproduced 5×

`row_blank()` is `mvwinnstr(wmsg, r, 0, …)`, which is `wmove` + `winnstr`. The row scan at `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:457-459` therefore leaves the `wmsg` cursor at **column 0 of the last non-blank row** before the guard at `tui.c:504` is reached. `main`'s gate returned *above* all of that (`tui.c:430` region), so it left the cursor where the echo had put it. `cursor_at_prompt` staying FALSE correctly suppresses the re-echo — but nothing suppresses the *player's next keystroke*, which lands at the parked cursor.

The sharpest case is a **width-only** drag, where nothing is lost and both question and answer stay on screen — the state the new `README.md`/`sst.doc` explicitly call safe ("carry on and answer"):

```
/tmp/verif_widthdrag.sh <sst> 600      # 600 -> 590 -> 600, then type one 'Z'

BRANCH:  23: Are you sure?
         24: Zbbbbbbbb…          <- the 'y' is gone from the screen
MAIN:    23: Are you sure?
         24: ybbbbbbbb…Z         <- appended, correct
```

The reader still holds `ybbb…`. The screen now shows an answer starting with `Z` while `ja()` will read the `y` — the exact "an `N` typed after a `y` you cannot see answers yes" hazard `sst.doc` warns about, in a state the new documentation declares safe.

Height drag, same mechanism: `/tmp/verif_wide.sh <sst> 600 24 Z` → `Zre you sure?` on the branch, `Are you sure?   …   Z` on `main`.

- **Threshold is exactly as designed**: COLS 513 (width 511) restores correctly and the `Z` appends after the answer; COLS 514 (width 512) fires the guard and corrupts. Confirmed at 514, 520, 600.
- **Root cause proven, not inferred**: a probe build (`/tmp/sst-mut4`) that saves `getcury/getcurx` before the row scan and restores them at the guard's return reproduces `main`'s behaviour exactly (`…bZ`).
- **Deterministic** — 5 runs across 3 widths, no variation.
- The comment at `tui.c:502-503`, "Leaving the screen alone is what this did before, and it is the safe end of the trade", is true of the screen and not of the cursor. Every other exit from the search block either returns having succeeded at `wmove` (`tui.c:602`) or falls through to the write path, which repositions; this guard is the only return that leaves the scan's cursor in place.

---

## Missing coverage

### 2. The guard itself is untested (this was the explicit mutation ask)

Deleting `tui.c:504` outright in a fresh copy of the working tree outside the repository (`/tmp/sst-mut`, `build/` left behind, reconfigured from scratch) and running `/tmp/sst-mut/tests/tui.sh /tmp/sst-mut/build/sst` gives **exit 0, "tui OK"** — the whole battery green with the blocker fix removed. The same binary under my out-of-repo repro at 600x24 shows the reviewer's failure (`questions=0` then `1`, answer rows going 1 → 2). `tests/tui.sh` never runs wider than 82 columns, so nothing in the repository can see this line.

### 3. The three "exact-fill" boundary guards are untested

Reverting all three at once — `skip % width == 0 ? skip : …` (`tui.c:533`), `ended && i % width != 0` (`tui.c:582`), `width <= 0 || linelen % width != 0` (`tui.c:701`) — in `/tmp/sst-mut3` leaves `tests/tui.sh` at **exit 0**. Nothing exercises a prompt that exactly fills its row (the tested message widths are 70/74/78 and " Are you sure? " divides none of them).

### 4. Coverage that *is* real (checked, not assumed)

- `arows` (`tui.c:479-482`): dropping `- arows` in `/tmp/sst-mut2` fails **3** assertions — `ended: after 80x23 …`, `wrapped answer: at 80x23 …`, `wrapped answer: at 76x24 …`. Genuinely covered.
- The new Enter assertion executed and passed: trace shows `+ wait_for 'It is stardate'` → `+ return 0` at `/tmp/tui-run2.trace:1758`.

### 5. Documentation now overstates the fix at ≥514 columns

`README.md` and `sst.doc:1550-1600` say the one remaining gap is "a window too short to hold the two", that the short window "keeps the answer and loses the question above it", and that growing the terminal brings the question back with your typing untouched. At ≥514 columns all three are wrong: the answer is lost and the **question** is what survives, and growing back to 24 rows does not recover it (`answerrows=0` at every step at 514 and 600). The loss itself is not a regression — `main` did the same — but the diff's own prose no longer describes it.

### 6. Minor

The Enter assertion proves the reader held a leading `y`; the other 86 characters are only asserted on screen. Adequate as layered, worth knowing.

---

## Answers to the four questions

- **Is `start < r` correct, and can it fire when it should not?** Correct, and no. `start` is clamped to ≥0 immediately above (`tui.c:485`), so `start < r` is exactly "≥2 rows joined". At width ≥ 512, `wantlen / width` is always 0 (`wantlen ≤ 381`: `curline[256]` plus a ≤126-char answer), so `start < r` ⟺ `arows ≥ 1` ⟺ ended with a non-empty answer. Confirmed empirically at 600 columns: the non-ended path (`COMMAND> srsc` + drag + type) restores and appends correctly, and the ended-with-nothing-typed path keeps the question exactly once with the `Z` landing on the row below. It never fires where `main` was already right.
- **Does returning leave anything in a bad state?** Yes — finding 1. `cursor_at_prompt = FALSE` is right and does what you expect (no double echo at `tui.c:966`); the cursor is the state that is wrong. Nothing else is mutated before the return (`getmaxy`/`getmaxx`/`snprintf` into a local).

```
MAIN:    23: Are you sure?
         24: ybbbbbbbb…Z         <- appended, correct
```

cd /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek
cat > "$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/i10.md" <<'EOF'
`restore_curline()`'s joined-row search reads each row with

```c
mvwinnstr(wmsg, rr, 0, onscreen, (int)sizeof onscreen - 1);
```

`onscreen` is 512 bytes, so it reads at most 511 columns. The search depends on
every appended row being *exactly* the window's width — that is what makes
`start`, `skip % width`, `bound` and `i / width` mean columns. Past 511 the rows
come back short, they stop lining up end to end, and the search misses a pair
that is perfectly intact.

The fix for #117 added a guard that returns rather than falling through, since
falling through stacks a copy of the question at every step of a drag. So at a
message window of 512 columns or more — a terminal of 514 — an ended prompt and
its part-typed answer are simply not restored.

## What a player sees

The same as before #117 at that width: on a height shrink the answer's row is
cut and the question's survives, so the screen reads as a clean unanswered
question while the reader still holds what was typed. `main` behaved the same
way, so this is not a regression — it is the one shape #117's fix does not
reach.

It is also why `sst.doc` and `README.md` say the line "usually" comes back
rather than that it does. The manual describes the short-window gap, which a
player can recognise on screen; it does not name a column count.

## How to see it

```sh
tmux -f /dev/null -L wide new-session -d -x 600 -y 24 './build/sst -t tournament 7 short novice pw'
# rest 5000, type y without Enter, then resize to -y 23 and back
```

At 513 columns the pair restores. At 514 it does not. `tests/tui.sh` covers the
guard itself at 600 columns — that the question is not duplicated and a
keystroke does not land on it — but nothing asserts a restore there, because
there is none to assert.

## Fix sketch

Two routes, and the second is the better one.

- Size the buffers from the terminal rather than fixing them at 512/2048.
  `restore_curline()` would need `onscreen` at `COLS` and `joined` at roughly
  four times that, which means allocating rather than declaring — the function
  is called on every repaint, so a static buffer grown on demand would suit it
  better than malloc per call.
- Stop joining rows at all. The search only needs to find the question and then
  look at what follows it, and the ended case already treats the answer as a
  separate string; comparing row by row would remove both the width dependence
  and the `joined` buffer. That is close to the second option #117's own fix
  sketch offered, carried one step further.

## Provenance

Found by `code-review` while reviewing the fix for #117, which made the path
reachable — an ended line's answer always has a row of its own, so the ended
case always joins more than one row, where nothing else at that width spans
two. Filed rather than fixed there: the buffers are a separate decision from
the two-row model, and 514 columns is far outside anything the manual
describes.
EOF
gh issue create --title "restore_curline() cannot restore a pair past 513 columns" --body-file "$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/i10.md"

content.text:
All checks are complete. Here is the report.

## 1. Verdict

**Pass** — every check ran and every check is green, on both build types, with sanitizers, and across five reruns of the TUI battery. No failures, no flakes.

One item under *Missing coverage* is a test added by this diff that passes vacuously; under `AGENTS.md` step 4 ("assert that the case it needs really occurred") that is yours to fix or resolve here rather than file, so read section 3 before committing.

## 2. Failures

None.

## 3. Your four questions

**Moving the guard above the row scan is correct and complete, and the cursor is exactly where `main` leaves it.**
The guard at `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:476` is preceded only by `getmaxy`/`getmaxx` and a `snprintf`, none of which move the cursor; `main`'s old gate returned from inside the `curlen == 0` block, also before any curses call that moves the cursor. Both leave `cursor_at_prompt` false. Proved rather than argued: full pane captures after the test's own sequence (600 cols, `y`, drag 23/24/23, type `Z`) are **byte-identical between the branch and a `main` build** (`/tmp/pane-branch-600.txt` vs `/tmp/pane-main-600.txt`), as are the captures at 514 columns. The failure I reported last round is gone — the exact repro (600 cols, 87-char `ybbb…` answer, width drag 600→590→600, type `Z`) now gives `Are you sure?` / `ybbb…Z` on both branch and `main`, and Enter still runs the rest.

**The early condition is equivalent to `start < r` at every reachable width, with one fragile premise worth a comment.**
`curline`/`lastline` are `char[256]` (`tui.c:284,298`) and the reader's echo is capped at `buflen-2` = 126 (`tui.c:938`). So for `width >= 512`: `wantlen <= 255` when `ended` (the answer is excluded from `want`) and `<= 381` otherwise, hence `wantlen / width == 0` always; `arows` is 1 iff `alen > 0` and 0 otherwise. `start < r` therefore reduces to exactly `ended && alen > 0`, which is the guard. No width differs. The threshold is also right, not off by one: `mvwinnstr` is given `sizeof onscreen - 1` = 511, so a row is complete iff `width <= 511`. Confirmed empirically at the boundary — 513 columns restores the pair correctly (`Are you sure?` / `yZ`, reader still holds the `y`), 514 does not and matches `main` exactly, which is precisely what #136 documents. The premise that could rot is `curline`'s 256 bytes, not the input buffer the comment names: raise `curline` past 511 and an ended line with an *empty* answer would join two rows at wide widths and slip past the guard. A word in the existing "Raise the input buffer and these want revisiting" note would cover it.

**The 600-column block is stable, and tmux at 600 is safe here.**
`tests/tui.sh` passed 5 clean runs (1 under `ctest -j 4`, 2 sequential, 3 concurrent under load) plus one under ASan/UBSan; the wide block never wavered. tmux 3.6 creates the detached 600x24 window without clamping — proved indirectly by the fact that the guard-deleted mutant *fails* at 600, which it could not do if the pane were narrower than 514. `start` exits hard if the session cannot be created, so a tmux that refused the size would fail loudly rather than skip. The script keeps its per-PID `-L` socket and `-f /dev/null`; no default-socket contact anywhere. Runtime cost: `tests/tui.sh` is 120s on the branch against 105s on `main`, well inside the 300s `TIMEOUT`.

**Nothing else in the diff assumes a row can be read whole, but one older assumption is now weaker than the new comment implies.**
At `width >= 512` with `ended && alen == 0`, or with a non-ended line, the code still joins a single *truncated* row (511 of 600 columns) and runs the tail-blank scan over it. That is harmless — content never passes column 381 and always starts at column 0 — and the column arithmetic is unaffected because `start == r`. The one to note is `row_blank()` (`tui.c:362`), which reads only 255 columns and has **no** guard at all; the new comment at `tui.c:411-416` ties the wholeness argument to `onscreen` and "the width guard there", which does not cover `row_blank`'s smaller buffer. I could not construct a reachable case (all written rows begin at column 0), so this is a latent note rather than a defect; #136 discusses `onscreen` only.

## 4. Missing coverage

**a. The new wide block passes with no answer typed at all — must-fix.** The block asserts nothing that requires the `y` to have reached the reader. With `tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'y'` replaced by a no-op in a copy of the tree, the **entire suite still passes** (`/tmp/vacuous.log`, exit 0). Without a pending answer the guard's condition is false, so the block exercises none of what it was added for, and both its assertions hold trivially: the question restores once through the ordinary path, and `Z` lands after it. Its neighbour, the wrapped-answer block, has exactly the control this lacks — it asserts the answer wrapped before dragging and presses Enter afterwards. Adding either here (assert `Are you sure?` with a `y` on the row below before the drags; or Enter + `wait_for 'It is stardate'` at the end) closes it.

**b. The cursor assertion is narrower than its message and comment claim.** It greps for `Zre you sure`, i.e. column 0 only. In the passing state the keystroke *does* land on the question, one column over: the screen reads `AZe you sure?`, and `main` produces the identical screen. So the message "a keystroke after the drag landed on the question" and the comment's "it is not what the display did before any of this" both overstate what is being distinguished — which is column 0 from column 1, the misplaced guard from `main` parity. The check is mechanically fine for the mutant it kills; the wording is what needs correcting, or the assertion needs to be about the question row's integrity relative to `main`'s known behaviour at ≥514 columns.

**c. No coverage at the 513/514 boundary.** Only 600 columns is exercised, so a mutant weakening the threshold to `width > (int)sizeof onscreen` would survive the suite while leaving a 514-column terminal duplicating the question. I verified both sides of the boundary by hand (513 restores, 514 matches `main`); nothing in the suite does.

**d. #135's two exact-fill guards are introduced by *this* diff**, not inherited — `main` has `if (ended) i = (i / width + 1) * width;` at `/tmp/mainsrc/tui.c:505` and `if (ended && maxy > 1)` at `:620`, both unconditional. Filing does not discharge a finding about new code (`AGENTS.md` step 9), so the "why filed rather than fixed" reasoning already written into #135 needs to appear as an explicit resolution in the PR body and the summary. I am not re-litigating the judgment; only noting where it has to be recorded. (Note also that #135's "nothing presses Enter after the drag" gap *was* fixed in this round — the issue is now partly stale.)

**Mutation results, all in a fresh copy at `/tmp/mut` with its own cache (`CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY:INTERNAL=/tmp/mut`):**

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| Guard moved back below the row scan | fails **only** `wide: a keystroke after the drag landed on the question` |
| Guard deleted | fails **only** `wide: at 600x23 the question is not on screen exactly once` |
| Erase padding line deleted (`total += oldmsgw - linelen % oldmsgw`) | fails `wrapped answer: at 76x24 …` — the diff's claim holds |

## Verdict: pass

Everything I ran is green, and every claim you asked me to check held up under mutation.

## What I checked, and the answers

**1. The new control (`tests/tui.sh:1587-1597`) — right, and it fires for its own reason.**
Reproduced your mutation in an out-of-repo copy (`rsync` excluding `.git`/`build*`, configured and built there): replacing `tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'y'` with `:` gives exactly one failure over the whole suite —
```
FAIL: wide: the answer never reached the reader, so the drags below prove nothing
1 check(s) failed.
```
Nothing else moved, which also confirms the drag counts and the `Z` check pass without an answer on screen.

It is a sound proxy for "reached the reader": in `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c` the echo happens only after the character is stored — `buf[len++] = (char)c; waddch(wmsg, c);` — so a `y` on screen means the reader holds it. The awk is correct in detail (uninitialised `q` compares equal to `0`; `capture-pane` strips trailing blanks and the `gsub` handles the leading one).

Ways it can fail other than the one it names — none of them make the block pass wrongly, but the message would misattribute:
- It really asserts *"the answer was echoed on the row below the question"*, which is both guard preconditions (`ended` shape **and** non-empty `pending_answer`). If the prompt stopped ending its own line, the failure would read as a lost keystroke.
- Fixed `sleep 1` rather than a poll after `send-keys`. Not observed in three full suite runs, and it matches its neighbours, so latent risk only.
- A dead capture (`screen` empty) lands on the same message via `q == 0`.

**2. The wide block exercises the guard on the paths it takes; height only.**
Two live mutants, each producing exactly one failure and nothing else:
- guard deleted (`tui.c:476-478`) → `FAIL: wide: at 600x23 the question is not on screen exactly once` — the first drag step, as the comment claims.
- guard moved below the row scan → `FAIL: wide: the guard ran after the row scan and moved the cursor to column 0`.

Gap: the drags are height-only. A guard narrowed to height-only resizes (`oldmsgw == 0 && width >= (int)sizeof onscreen && ...`) leaves the whole suite green (`tui OK`). I then drove that mutant by hand over a width drag at 600 columns (596/592/588/584) and the screen was indistinguishable from the fixed build — question count 1 at every step — which matches `tests/tui.sh:1272-1275` ("a missed match there costs a rewrite, not a copy"). So it reads as an equivalent mutant on the width branch, not a hole. Noted, not a must-fix.

**3. The corrected cursor wording matches what the check distinguishes.**
Hand-driven wide journey, branch build: after `Z` the row is `AZe you sure?`, `Zre you sure` count 0. Same journey against a build with `main`'s `tui.c`: identical — `AZe you sure?`, and the drag counts are 1 at each step there too. So the check separates column 0 from column 1 and nothing else, exactly as the comment now says, while still being the sole detector of the relocation mutant.

**4. `README.md` — no meaning lost, and the meaning is true.**
The pre-rewrap state was never committed, so there is no artefact to diff against; I checked the current text against `main`'s text and against the game instead. Every claim holds, at 80 columns with an 87-character part-typed answer:
- 80x16 — question and wrapped answer both on screen.
- 80x15 — `ybbb…` whole, question gone ("the answer is what survives").
- 80x14 — a fragment of the answer only ("shorter still only part of that").
- 80x15 → 80x17 — `Are you sure?` back with the typing untouched, and `Enter` then acted on it ("give the terminal another row or two first").

Longest added line is 72 characters (`Only their final line comes back…`; the `on and answer —` line is 70), so nothing exceeds 73. `sst.doc` carries the same paragraph and agrees with it and with behaviour; its page 27 grows 128→134 lines, but that page was already the longest in the file, so no new invariant.

## Failures
None. No flakes: three independent `tests/tui.sh` runs (standalone, Debug `ctest`, Release `ctest`) all green.

## Missing coverage
- **The documented too-short-window states are asserted nowhere.** `README.md` and `sst.doc` now promise that when the window cannot hold the pair, the *answer* is what survives; the suite only checks the recovered state after growing back to 80x24. A future change that kept the question and dropped the answer would leave both documents wrong and a player typing over a hidden `y`, with the suite green. This is behaviour this diff introduces and documents, so it wants a test or an explicit resolution rather than an issue.
- Width drags at ≥512 columns (above) — probably equivalent, worth one sentence wherever the height-only choice is recorded.
- #136's 513/514 boundary: not re-measured this round, per your note that it is recorded there.

## Environment issues
- No `cppcheck`, `clang-tidy`, `scan-build`, `clang` or `valgrind` on this machine, so the only static analysis was gcc's. `shellcheck` is present: `shellcheck -s sh tests/tui.sh` is clean (exit 0).
- Both builds were configured with `-DSST_WERROR=ON` even though `verifier.md` does not ask for it (#125): clean, zero warnings, Debug and Release.
- `/tmp` here is a **shared 61G tmpfs that hit 100% mid-run** (other agents' scratch plus my own 918M `cp -a` of the repo). It killed my first `tests/tui.sh` run — empty log, exit 1 — and broke the shell until I freed space. That run is discarded, not counted; everything reported is from runs after the disk was freed, and later copies used `rsync --exclude '.git' --exclude 'build*'`. Do not `cp -a` this repo into `/tmp`.
- One tmux server exists on the *default* socket (`difftest`), owned by you. Untouched. All my sessions used private `-L` sockets killed by their own traps; I removed the seven dead socket files this session left in `/tmp/tmux-1000/`.
- Repo left exactly as I found it: `git status` still shows only `README.md`, `sst.doc`, `tests/tui.sh`, `tui.c` modified, same diffstat.

## What ran
- `cmake -S . -B /tmp/vb-debug -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DSST_WERROR=ON && cmake --build /tmp/vb-debug` — clean.
- `cmake -S . -B /tmp/vb-release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSST_WERROR=ON && cmake --build /tmp/vb-release` — clean.
- `ctest` in both build dirs — 11/11 passed each (Debug 266s, Release 257s), including `tui`, `golden`, `tournament`.
- `sh tests/tui.sh /tmp/vb-debug/sst Debug` standalone — `tui OK` (2m00s).
- `shellcheck -s sh tests/tui.sh`.
- Plain-mode journey compared against a `main`-`tui.c` build, deterministically: `printf 'srscan\nstatus\nrest 5000\ny\nchart\nquit\ny\n' | sst tournament 7 short novice` — byte-identical output.

Plus the wrapped block's own `'ybbb'` mutation, which fails on both of its checks as its comment claims.
- Hand-driven tmux journeys on private sockets: wide 600x24 height drag + `Z` on branch and on `main`; 600-column width drag on branch and on the height-only mutant; 80x24→20/16/15/14 with one-character and wrapping answers; 80x15→17→24 grow-back followed by `Enter`.

```
13  mqqq...j mqqq...j          <- panel bottom borders
14   ybbbbbb...(78 cols)
```

The height is not on a knife edge. I walked the boundary by hand: 16 rows shows the whole pair (question + two answer rows, exact fit), 15 shows the answer alone, 14 shows only the tail (`bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`), which is the "shorter still only a piece of that is left" case both documents describe. 15 is the only height that produces the state the assertion names.

Given the current layout — an ended prompt's answer starts a row of its own — a 2-row window and a 3-row pair force the question off, and any build that re-echoes the whole answer must push it away. Both documents say so on disk (`sst.doc:1582` onward, "a window left too short to hold the pair keeps the answer and loses the question above it"; `README.md`, "the answer is what survives").

What is *not* forced is the 3-row layout. A build that packed the pair onto the two rows would show `Are you sure? ybbb…` / `bbb…` — question and answer both visible, nothing lost, arguably better for the player — and would be judged wrong only because `sst.doc` and `README.md` now promise otherwise. That is the assertion doing its job (it is the thing that would make a future UI change update the docs too), but it means "correct" here is a documentation contract, not a law of the display.

  ```c
  if (ended && maxy > 1 && (width <= 0 || linelen % width != 0))
  ```

That is the "opposite" the comment says it could not construct, it is a game break rather than a test break, and this block is the only thing in the suite that sees it.

**Both of my previous findings are properly answered.** The width guard is correct at the boundary: `mvwinnstr` is called with `sizeof onscreen - 1` = 511, so a row is short exactly when `width >= 512`, which is what the guard tests. I confirmed your equivalence claim rather than taking it — at `width >= 512`, `wantlen` cannot exceed 381 (`curline` 255 + a 126-byte answer), so `wantlen / width` is always 0 and `arows` is 0 or 1; the only case that joins more than one row is an ended line with a non-empty answer, which is exactly the guard's condition. Placing it above the `row_blank` scan is right — that is the only cursor-moving call before it, and `sync_size()` sets `cursor_at_prompt = FALSE` before the repaint, so the early return leaves the reader non-echoing, which is what `main` did. The `arows`/`start` correction, the padding-and-prefix skip, and the three exact-fill guards all hold for the shapes I traced (empty answer, NULL answer at a pause, height-cut answer row, exact-fill question at the window's last row). `joined` cannot overflow: the worst case is about 1022 bytes at `width` 511, well inside 2048.

## Findings

### should-fix — `sst.doc:1583-1592`, `README.md:54-64`: the manual now tells the player the wrong half survives, and gives a remedy that does not work, in exactly the state this diff's own guard creates

`sst.doc:1585` says "a window left too short to hold the pair keeps the answer and loses the question above it", and `README.md:54` calls that "The gap left". At a message window of 512 columns or more — the case your new guard returns from, and which `main` also could not restore — the reverse happens. I reproduced it at 600x24 with `tournament 7 short novice pw`:

```
=== before ===          === after -y 23 ===     === after -y 24 ===
 COMMAND> rest 5000      COMMAND> rest 5000      COMMAND> rest 5000
 Are you sure?           Are you sure?           Are you sure?
 y
```

The question is kept and the answer is lost — a clean unanswered question with the reader still holding `y`. That is the precise shape the paragraph exists to warn against: the player types `N`, `ja()` reads the `y`, and for the self-destruct or an "are you sure" that ends a game, that is the game. The old text covered it ("A question you had already begun answering may not come back at all... If either is missing, do not answer and do not press Enter"); the new text drops the unconditional caution and routes the player instead to `sst.doc:1589` — "give the terminal another row or two before anything else: the question comes back with your typing untouched" — which is false here, and leaves no exit, since the terminal *can* grow.

`#136` says the word "usually" is what carries this. "Usually" covers *whether* the line returns; it does not cover *which half* is missing, and it does not make the grow-the-terminal remedy true. The fix is a clause, not a rewrite, and needs no column count: make the missing half either way round ("whichever of the two is missing"), and condition the Ctrl-U advice on failure as well as on an immovable terminal — "If it does not come back, or the terminal cannot grow, do not answer and do not press Enter". Same two changes in `README.md`.

I verified this edit does not itself reach the player: `sst.c:159-200` only prints `sst.doc` topics between a `Mnemonic:` header and `******`, and the changed region is in "Modifications I made", outside any topic.

### should-fix — review-coverage claim is incomplete for `ui-review`

You gave me counts ("`ui-review` three") but not the one thing step 8 asks for: whether the last `ui-review` round saw the state being committed. It matters here specifically. The width guard at `tui.c:476` did not exist when I raised it as a blocker, so it postdates at least my second `code-review` round, and it was then *moved* after the `verifier` failed its first placement. Both the guard and its placement are player-visible — the guard decides whether the pair is restored at all, and its placement decides where the next keystroke lands. If `ui-review` round three predates the guard, the newest player-facing behavior in this diff has had no screen-reading pass.

I am not asking for a rerun on principle: the post-round-three player-visible delta is confined to windows of 512+ columns, where the outcome is "unchanged from `main`", and that is a defensible argument. But make it, with the round's verdict and what it says it exercised, rather than leaving it to a count. If instead round three did see the current `tui.c`, say so and this is answered as-is.

## On the #135 resolution — accepted

You are recording it as a resolution rather than a filing, which is the right call now that you have confirmed both guards are introduced by this diff. The substance holds up on my own check: `ended` requires `curlen == 0 && reader_waiting`, and a pause keeps `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` in `curline`, so the ended set really is prompts that finish their line before a reader. The longest `prout` literals in the tree are 86, 72 and 71 characters, and the 86 is `"Spock- \"Captain, the Treaty of Algeron is in effect.\n   Are you sure this is wise?\""` — the embedded `\n` means `lastline` is the 30-character tail, not the whole thing. Nothing reaches 70. Your framing of the watch item is the correct one: a future `prout` literal of 70+ characters written immediately before a reader, not a terminal width.

## Not reviewed

- I did not run `ui-review`; that is not this pass, and reading code is not reading screens.
- I could not check what `ui-review` round three actually covered — hence the finding above.
- The intermediate-width answer-wholeness gap (76/72) left open in #135 is deferred by that issue and I did not re-litigate it.

Both the guard and its placement are player-visible — the guard decides whether the pair is restored at all, and its placement decides where the next keystroke lands. I am not asking for a rerun on principle: the post-round-three player-visible delta is confined to windows of 512+ columns, where the outcome is "unchanged from `main`", and that is a defensible argument. You are recording it as a resolution rather than a filing, which is the right call now that you have confirmed both guards are introduced by this diff. The substance holds up on my own check: `ended` requires `curlen == 0 && reader_waiting`, and a pause keeps `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` in `curline`, so the ended set really is prompts that finish their line before a reader.
