## Verdict

Acceptable as-is on behaviour; the documentation needs one more pass. Driven at 72, 76, 80, 260–300, 513, 514 and 600 columns and from 13 to 24 rows, the code as it now stands is sound: at every ordinary size the question and its part-typed answer come back exactly once with the cursor sitting after the answer, a wrapping 87-character answer survives two-dimensional dragging, the self-destruct password survives a drag and is still accepted, and plain mode is byte-identical to `main` on a deterministic journey. At 512+ columns the new guard does exactly what it claims: the screen is left untouched, the cursor is *not* moved to column 0, and I could not tell the branch from `main` in any wide-terminal journey I ran — including width drags, which turn out to be fine at those widths (the pair stays put and typing continues correctly), so only a height shrink that cuts the answer's row loses anything. The remaining findings are all in the rewritten `sst.doc`/`README.md` passages: they now name the wide-terminal case but attribute it to a window that "cannot hold the pair", send the player to a remedy that provably never works there, and have dropped the old warning about the state where *neither* half comes back — which I reproduced at 600x18 and which persists after growing back.

## Findings

**1. should-fix — `sst.doc:1551-1557`, `sst.doc:1582-1589`, `README.md:54-59`: the cause given for the wide-terminal case is the opposite of the truth.**
Both files say the loss happens because the window "cannot hold the pair" / is "too short to hold that and your answer both", and then, in the same sentence, name the very-wide terminal as a case of it. At 600x24 the message window is ten rows and holds the pair easily; it is lost anyway, because the restore declines to run. The `sst.doc` summary paragraph is the worse of the two, since it gives only the short-window cause and a player on a wide terminal will read it as not applying to them. What I saw: 600x24, `rest 5000`, type `y`, shrink to 23 and back — question alone, answer gone for good.
Suggestion: separate cause from symptom, e.g. `sst.doc:1553-1556` "It can still cost you the question you were part way through answering, or the answer itself on a very wide terminal — which is what the last of these paragraphs is about", and in the long paragraph "…because you may get back only one of the two. Usually the window is too short to hold the pair and the question is what goes; on a very wide terminal it is the answer, however tall the window is."

**2. should-fix — `sst.doc:1591-1594`, `README.md:61-64`: "give the terminal another row or two first" never works at the wide end, and the thing that does work is not mentioned.**
This is the first remedy both documents offer, and at ≥ ~514 columns it is precisely the one action that cannot help: I dragged 600x23↔24 repeatedly and the answer never returned at any height. What *does* bring it back with the typing intact is making the terminal *narrower* — 600 → 400 restored the answer under its question, once, cursor after it. A player following the current text on a 4K terminal grows the window several times, gets nothing, and only then reaches the Ctrl-U paragraph (which does work there: I ran C-u, `n`, Enter at 600 columns and the rest was correctly declined).
Suggestion: name the exception where the remedy is given — "…another row or two first: that usually brings it back with your typing untouched. A very wide terminal is the exception: more rows will not bring the answer back, though making the terminal narrower will."

**3. should-fix — `sst.doc:1582-1589`, `README.md:54-59`: the case where *neither* half comes back is no longer described, and the old warning about it was removed in this diff.**
The previous text said "A question you had already begun answering may not come back at all, and what you are then looking at may be older conversation that reads exactly like a live prompt." The new text says the window "drops one half or the other" and "only a piece of whichever survived is left" — which implies something always survives. It does not: at 600x24 with `y` typed, shrinking to 18 rows and growing back to 24 leaves the message window holding briefing text and then nothing at all, with the reader still waiting and the cursor parked in the middle of a stale line. Same on `main`, so it is not a regression, but it is the state a player is most likely to misread as "the game is idle", and it is now the one screen the manual does not describe. (The advice still routes correctly via "If either is missing", so this is about the description, not the instructions.)
Suggestion: restore one sentence after "Shorter still and only a piece of whichever survived is left" — "and sometimes neither comes back, leaving older conversation on screen with the game waiting behind it."

**4. nit — `tui.c` width guard, wide terminals: the caret is left inside the question, so the first keystroke overwrites it.**
At 600 columns after the answer is lost, the cursor sits at column 1 of the question row; typing `Z` produces ` AZe you sure?`, and on the self-destruct prompt typing the rest of the password produced ` SELF-uctoRUCT-SEQUENCE-WILL-BE-ABORTED` (the password was still accepted). Byte-for-byte identical to `main`, and #136 covers the underlying non-restore, so nothing to change in this slice — worth adding to #136 as the player-visible symptom, since it is the one place the screen actively mis-renders rather than merely omits.

**5. nit — `tui.c:476-478`: the guard is slightly broader than the failure it prevents.**
It fires on width alone, so at 600x14 — where the message window is one row and the question and answer share it, and the single-row join would have been fine — the restore is skipped as well. Harmless (nothing garbles; Enter still submits the held answer, which I confirmed), and narrowing the condition is not worth doing here. Worth a line on #136.

## What I exercised

- Built Debug and read the whole of `restore_curline()` plus `tui_readline()`'s resize branch; read the full diff of `tui.c`, `tests/tui.sh`, `sst.doc`, `README.md`.
- Ordinary sizes: 80x24 and 72x24 setup-question drags (part-typed `tourn`), 72x24 full journey (setup → srscan → move → quit → score prompt with a part-typed `y` dragged across four sizes), 80x24 `rest 5000` / `Are you sure?` with a one-character answer dragged down to 14 rows and back, and an 11-step two-dimensional drag (80x23 → 72x19 → 80x24 → 80x16 → 80x24) counting question and answer occurrences at every step — exactly one of each throughout, cursor always immediately after the answer; Enter then submitted the held answer.
- Wrapping answer (87 chars) at 80 and 72 columns: verified the wrap, dragged width 80→72→80 and height 24→13→24, confirmed the documented 80x15/72x15 state (answer kept, question dropped), the 80x14 fragment ("only part of whichever survived"), 80x13 (nothing), and full recovery at 80x24.

## Verdict

Acceptable as-is on behaviour; the documentation needs one more pass. Driven at 72, 76, 80, 260–300, 513, 514 and 600 columns and from 13 to 24 rows, the code as it now stands is sound: at every ordinary size the question and its part-typed answer come back exactly once with the cursor sitting after the answer, a wrapping 87-character answer survives two-dimensional dragging, the self-destruct password survives a drag and is still accepted, and plain mode is byte-identical to `main` on a deterministic journey. At 512+ columns the new guard does exactly what it claims: the screen is left untouched, the cursor is *not* moved to column 0, and I could not tell the branch from `main` in any wide-terminal journey I ran — including width drags, which turn out to be fine at those widths (the pair stays put and typing continues correctly), so only a height shrink that cuts the answer's row loses anything. The remaining findings are all in the rewritten `sst.doc`/`README.md` passages: they now name the wide-terminal case but attribute it to a window that "cannot hold the pair", send the player to a remedy that provably never works there, and have dropped the old warning about the state where *neither* half comes back — which I reproduced at 600x18 and which persists after growing back.

## Findings

**1. should-fix — `sst.doc:1551-1557`, `sst.doc:1582-1589`, `README.md:54-59`: the cause given for the wide-terminal case is the opposite of the truth.**
Both files say the loss happens because the window "cannot hold the pair" / is "too short to hold that and your answer both", and then, in the same sentence, name the very-wide terminal as a case of it. At 600x24 the message window is ten rows and holds the pair easily; it is lost anyway, because the restore declines to run. The `sst.doc` summary paragraph is the worse of the two, since it gives only the short-window cause and a player on a wide terminal will read it as not applying to them. What I saw: 600x24, `rest 5000`, type `y`, shrink to 23 and back — question alone, answer gone for good.
Suggestion: separate cause from symptom, e.g. `sst.doc:1553-1556` "It can still cost you the question you were part way through answering, or the answer itself on a very wide terminal — which is what the last of these paragraphs is about", and in the long paragraph "…because you may get back only one of the two. Usually the window is too short to hold the pair and the question is what goes; on a very wide terminal it is the answer, however tall the window is."

**2. should-fix — `sst.doc:1591-1594`, `README.md:61-64`: "give the terminal another row or two first" never works at the wide end, and the thing that does work is not mentioned.**
This is the first remedy both documents offer, and at ≥ ~514 columns it is precisely the one action that cannot help: I dragged 600x23↔24 repeatedly and the answer never returned at any height. What *does* bring it back with the typing intact is making the terminal *narrower* — 600 → 400 restored the answer under its question, once, cursor after it. A player following the current text on a 4K terminal grows the window several times, gets nothing, and only then reaches the Ctrl-U paragraph (which does work there: I ran C-u, `n`, Enter at 600 columns and the rest was correctly declined).
Suggestion: name the exception where the remedy is given — "…another row or two first: that usually brings it back with your typing untouched. A very wide terminal is the exception: more rows will not bring the answer back, though making the terminal narrower will."

**3. should-fix — `sst.doc:1582-1589`, `README.md:54-59`: the case where *neither* half comes back is no longer described, and the old warning about it was removed in this diff.**
The previous text said "A question you had already begun answering may not come back at all, and what you are then looking at may be older conversation that reads exactly like a live prompt." The new text says the window "drops one half or the other" and "only a piece of whichever survived is left" — which implies something always survives. It does not: at 600x24 with `y` typed, shrinking to 18 rows and growing back to 24 leaves the message window holding briefing text and then nothing at all, with the reader still waiting and the cursor parked in the middle of a stale line. Same on `main`, so it is not a regression, but it is the state a player is most likely to misread as "the game is idle", and it is now the one screen the manual does not describe. (The advice still routes correctly via "If either is missing", so this is about the description, not the instructions.)
Suggestion: restore one sentence after "Shorter still and only a piece of whichever survived is left" — "and sometimes neither comes back, leaving older conversation on screen with the game waiting behind it."

**4. nit — `tui.c` width guard, wide terminals: the caret is left inside the question, so the first keystroke overwrites it.**
At 600 columns after the answer is lost, the cursor sits at column 1 of the question row; typing `Z` produces ` AZe you sure?`, and on the self-destruct prompt typing the rest of the password produced ` SELF-uctoRUCT-SEQUENCE-WILL-BE-ABORTED` (the password was still accepted). Byte-for-byte identical to `main`, and #136 covers the underlying non-restore, so nothing to change in this slice — worth adding to #136 as the player-visible symptom, since it is the one place the screen actively mis-renders rather than merely omits.

**5. nit — `tui.c:476-478`: the guard is slightly broader than the failure it prevents.**
It fires on width alone, so at 600x14 — where the message window is one row and the question and answer share it, and the single-row join would have been fine — the restore is skipped as well. Harmless (nothing garbles; Enter still submits the held answer, which I confirmed), and narrowing the condition is not worth doing here. Worth a line on #136.

- Built Debug and read the whole of `restore_curline()` plus `tui_readline()`'s resize branch; read the full diff of `tui.c`, `tests/tui.sh`, `sst.doc`, `README.md`.

The line you were on usually comes back with the panels, and so does
  whatever you had typed of an answer to it -- but look at both before
  you touch the keyboard, because you may get back only one of them.
  Usually the window is too short to hold the pair and the question is
  what goes, leaving you looking at what you typed with nothing on
  screen to say what it answers; on a very wide terminal it is the
  answer that goes instead, however tall the window is, leaving a
  question that looks as though nothing had been typed at all. Shorter
  still and only a piece of whichever survived is left, and sometimes
  neither comes back, leaving older conversation on screen with the
  game waiting behind it. If the question and everything you had typed
  are both on screen, carry on. If either is missing, give the
  terminal another row or two before anything else: that usually
  brings it back with your typing untouched, which beats retyping it
  -- the self-destruct password can be nine characters. A very wide
  terminal is the exception: more rows will not bring the answer back
  there, though making the terminal narrower will. If it does not come
  back, or the terminal cannot grow, do not answer and do not press
  Enter: press Ctrl-U first, which throws the line away. What you
  typed is still in it unseen, and a yes/no question reads the first
  word of your answer and only its first letter, so an "N" typed after
  a "y" you cannot see answers yes -- and some of those questions can
  end the game. With the line cleared, Enter is safe, since nothing
  waiting behind a prompt commits you to anything. A yes/no question
  then asks again only as Please answer with "Y" or "N", never
  repeating what it wanted; answer N to decline whatever it was.

Only nits below, so per your standing decision they can be recorded in the PR body rather than edited.

### What I checked this round

The two things I asked for are answered, and answered by evidence rather than by argument:

I verified the claims they now make against the code and the tests: the short-window case (question goes, answer survives) is what `restore_curline()` produces and is what `tests/tui.sh` asserts at 80x15; the wide case is the new `width >= (int)sizeof onscreen` guard returning before anything is restored, which leaves `cursor_at_prompt` false so no echo happens either — behaviour identical to `main` above that width, which is exactly what round 4 reported being unable to distinguish. "Narrowing brings it back" follows from crossing back under the guard into the `oldmsgw > 0` erase-and-rewrite branch.
- **Review coverage.** Four `ui-review` rounds with the last one seeing the current `tui.c`, and the coverage named — 72/76/80/260-300/513/514/600 columns, 13-24 rows — maps onto branches the diff actually has rather than onto journeys it cannot reach. 513 vs 514 is the right boundary and it lands where the code puts it: `restore_curline(COLS != oldcols ? oldcols - 2 : 0)` makes the message window `COLS - 2`, so 513 gives width 511 (a full row from `mvwinnstr` into `onscreen[512]`) and 514 gives 512 (short row). That is a verdict plus a list I could check, not "it ran".

I also re-derived the arithmetic rather than trusting the comments: `arows`/`start` cannot push `joined` past 2048 at any reachable width; `bound` and the prefix `strncmp` are in-bounds in every branch, including when `joined` ends before `bound` because a height shrink cut the answer's row (`skip < bound` at the NUL, prefix check skipped, tail scan terminates immediately, `tail_blank` stays true); the erase-path `total` rounding gives the same row count as `ceil(linelen/oldmsgw) + ceil(alen/oldmsgw)`, including the empty-`pending_answer` case; and `scrollok(wmsg, TRUE)` at `tui.c:258` is what makes suppressing the newline correct when `linelen % width == 0`.

### Findings

**Nit — `tui.c:698`**: the comment "the erase below has a fourth" points the wrong way and miscounts. The erase's guard is `if (ended && pending_answer != NULL && linelen % oldmsgw != 0)` at `tui.c:639`, which is *above* line 698, not below it; and since the four occurrences of this guard are the padding skip, the cursor rounding, the erase, and this one, the guard at 704 *is* the fourth. A maintainer taking the comment at its word looks below line 704 for a fourth guard and finds the end of the function. Suggested fix: "The last of the same guard — the erase above has the third —". The two adjacent block comments at 693-697 and 698-703 are fine as they stand; that doubling is the file's own idiom (see 572-584).

**Nit — `README.md:68` and `sst.doc:1597`**: "though making the terminal narrower will" is unqualified, and narrowing is only a remedy once you cross back under the threshold. A player on a 600-column terminal who drags to 550 finds the answer still gone and the advice wrong. Both files elsewhere are willing to name a column count ("Narrower than 72 columns…"), so this is not a case where the number is off-limits — but it is a buffer size rather than a game rule, so "narrow enough" or "much narrower" would carry the same warning without pinning it. Round 4 tested 600 → 400, which does not distinguish the two wordings.

### Not reviewed

- I could not verify the `ui-review` and `verifier` round counts themselves, only that the state I read is the state the described round 4 findings were made against — the three documentation rewrites and the width guard are all present in the worktree as described.
- The claim that at 600x24 shrunk to 18 rows and back *neither* half returns is empirical; I confirmed it is consistent with the code (guard returns, nothing rewritten, the height shrink already cut the rows) but did not drive a terminal to reproduce it.
- #135 and #136 are your filings; I did not read the issue tracker.

fix(tui): restore an ended prompt together with a part-typed answer

restore_curline() refused to put back a prompt that had ended its own
line once the player had begun typing an answer. The gate was
deliberate: two earlier attempts at spanning the row boundary between
an ended prompt and its answer each duplicated the question instead,
once per width step the first time and once on a one-row height shrink
the second.

What it left is worse than either at one shape. wresize() cuts the
answer's row and keeps the question's, so a one-row height shrink
leaves the screen reading as a clean unanswered question while the
reader still holds the typed y. Reproduced: type N there and the game
submits yN, ja() takes the y, rest 5000 runs, and it ends with "Your
time has run out and the Federation has been conquered."

The comparison now models two rows rather than one, which is the
second of the two routes the issue sketched. want is the question
alone for an ended line, since a single joined string can only match
all or none of a pair the shrink has halved. The read-back steps back
over every row the answer takes. The tail test steps over curses'
padding and then over as much of the answer as is on screen -- a
prefix, because the shrink truncates it -- before asking whether the
rest is blank. Three places that rounded up to the next row boundary
unconditionally are guarded for a question that fills its row exactly.

It restores the display and does not discard the buffered y: typing N
after a resize still answers yes. That is the player's to clear and
the manual says how. What the fix buys is that they can see there is
something to clear.

A width guard came out of review. Past 511 columns mvwinnstr reads a
short row, the joined rows stop lining up, and the tail test fails
against a pair that is intact -- after which the write path stacks a
copy at every step. Only an ended line joins more than one row at that
width, so this change is what made it reachable. It returns instead,
which is what the display did before, and it sits above the row scan
because that scan moves the cursor: returning past it parked the next
keystroke on the question. Filed as 136, and why both documents now
say the line usually comes back.

to press Ctrl-U and retype an answer that is now intact, the
self-destruct password included. Both now say what survives at each
end -- usually the question goes and the answer stays, on a very wide
terminal the reverse, and sometimes neither -- and give growing the
terminal as the first remedy, with narrowing it as the one that works
at the wide end.

The test asserted only that the question was never on screen more than
once, which tolerated zero. It now asserts the pair, and a second
block drags a wrapping answer through four heights and four widths,
checks it wrapped before proving anything with it, checks the too-short
state the documents describe, and presses Enter to prove the reader
holds what the screen shows. A third covers the width guard at 600
columns.
